Mobility Lens
Mobile apps have to work in situations that desktop apps usually don\'t\nMove through the six dimensions below to see what a developer should think about

Input and interaction
Phones mainly rely on touch, so users don\'t have the same precision they would get from a mouse or keyboard
Buttons and other controls should be easy to tap and important actions shouldn\'t depend on tiny targets or precise movements
Screen size, orientation, and density
A phone has limited screen space and the layout can change when the device rotates or runs on a different screen size
The interface should focus on what matters most and should still be usable when the screen size or orientation changes
Lifecycle and resource constraints
A mobile app can be paused, stopped, recreated or removed from memory while the user moves between apps
Developers shouldn\'t assume the app will stay running, important state should be saved when losing it would interrupt the user
Context awareness
Phones move with the user and can react to things like location, movement, connectivity and the surrounding environment
Context can make an app more useful but developers should only use information that actually helps the feature and should handle unavailable data
Usage patterns
People often use mobile apps in short sessions while walking, commuting, waiting or doing something else at the same time
Common tasks should be quick to understand and finish without making the user go through unnecessary steps
Security and privacy expectations
Phones can contain personal information and are easily carried, shared, misplaced or stolen
An app should only collect information it needs, protect sensitive data and avoid requesting permissions without a clear reason
